The patient presents with B-symptoms, a fixed painless neck mass, and neurological symptoms, none of which are characteristic of gallbladder inflammation. My initial assessment of Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma remains a strong possibility given the smoking history, but the lack of primary lung or head/neck mass on imaging makes a primary lymphoma more probable.

Doctor 2: I agree with Doctor 1. Cholecystitis is inconsistent with the clinical picture. The triad of B-symptoms (night sweats, weight loss, fatigue) combined with a fixed, painless cervical lymph node is the classic presentation of a hematologic malignancy. The normal imaging of the chest and abdomen further supports a diagnosis centered in the lymphatic system rather than a solid organ pathology like carcinoma or cholecystitis. Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma fits the data best.
